edge.label: Path traversal file download enables exfiltration of Linux credential stores (/etc/shadow, password hashes) or application config files, verifying or extracting default 'pi:raspberry' credentials to obtain administrator privileges.

source_node.label: piSignage Arbitrary File Download via Log Path Traversal (api/settings/log)
source_node.precondition: Remote network access and low-privilege authenticated user credentials for the piSignage player web application (version < 2.6.4) on a Raspberry Pi device.
source_node.postcondition: Download of arbitrary local files across the Raspberry Pi file system via the 'api/settings/log?file=../' parameter traversal, exposing sensitive configurations, source code, and stored system credentials.

target_node.label: Raspberry Pi OS Default Credentials Administrator Access
target_node.precondition: Network reachability (e.g., SSH, local login, or service console) to Raspberry Pi OS (version <= 5.10) where the factory default credentials for account 'pi' with password 'raspberry' remain unchanged.
target_node.postcondition: Attacker acquires administrator (sudo/root) privileges and unrestricted control over the Raspberry Pi operating system and resident applications.

source_evidence.description: The web application component of piSignage before 2.6.4 allows a remote attacker (authenticated as a low-privilege user) to download arbitrary files from the Raspberry Pi via api/settings/log?file=../ path traversal. In other words, this issue is in the player API for log download.
Raspberry Pi OS through 5.10 has the raspberry default password for the pi account. If not changed, attackers can gain administrator privileges.

edge.label: Arbitrary file download allows extraction of RaspAP configuration, session databases, or cleartext credentials from the filesystem, fulfilling the authenticated access precondition for the misconfigured web console.

target_node.label: RaspAP Misconfigured Web Console Command Execution (includes/webconsole.php)
target_node.precondition: Network access and authenticated user access to RaspAP (version 2.5) web application hosting 'includes/webconsole.php' on the Raspberry Pi.
target_node.postcondition: Unrestricted command execution on the underlying Raspberry Pi operating system, enabling arbitrary file uploads, shell code execution, and lateral compromise of system services.

source_evidence.description: The web application component of piSignage before 2.6.4 allows a remote attacker (authenticated as a low-privilege user) to download arbitrary files from the Raspberry Pi via api/settings/log?file=../ path traversal. In other words, this issue is in the player API for log download.

An issue was discovered in includes/webconsole.php in RaspAP 2.5. With authenticated access, an attacker can use a misconfigured (and virtually unrestricted) web console to attack the underlying OS (Raspberry Pi) running this software, and execute commands on the system (including ones for uploading of files and execution of code).

edge.label: Executing commands on the underlying OS allows an attacker to interact with the local shell, leveraging unhardened default 'pi' account credentials or sudo rules to escalate to full administrator status.

edge.label: Potential code execution achieved via Oculus Browser UI injection provides the initial local unprivileged Windows execution context required to craft log hard links and trigger OVRRedir.exe arbitrary file write.

source_node.label: Oculus Browser Arbitrary HTML UI Injection and Potential Code Execution
source_node.precondition: Target user browsing the web using Oculus Browser (versions 5.2.7 through 5.7.11) visits an attacker-controlled remote web page.
source_node.postcondition: Arbitrary HTML injected into the Oculus Browser user interface, facilitating UI spoofing, credential phishing, and potential code execution in the context of an unprivileged local user session.

target_node.label: Oculus Desktop OVRRedir.exe Privileged File Write Local Privilege Escalation
target_node.precondition: Unprivileged local process execution on a Windows host running Oculus Desktop (version < 1.44.0.32849) capable of creating file-system hard links to log files targeted by OVRRedir.exe.
target_node.postcondition: Arbitrary file write with the elevated permissions of the privileged OVRRedir.exe process, resulting in full local privilege escalation to Administrator or SYSTEM on Windows.

source_evidence.description: A remote web page could inject arbitrary HTML code into the Oculus Browser UI, allowing an attacker to spoof UI and potentially execute code. This affects the Oculus Browser starting from version 5.2.7 until 5.7.11.

Writing to an unprivileged file from a privileged OVRRedir.exe process in Oculus Desktop before 1.44.0.32849 on Windows allows local users to write to arbitrary files and consequently gain privileges via vectors involving a hard link to a log file.

edge.label: Initial unprivileged code execution achieved via the browser engine allows an attacker to execute as a local unprivileged process to query and acquire exposed privileged handles from OVRServiceLauncher.exe.

target_node.label: Oculus Desktop OVRServiceLauncher.exe Handle Exposure Local Privilege Escalation
target_node.precondition: Unprivileged local process running on a Windows host with Oculus Desktop (version > 1.39 and < 31.1.0.67.507) where OVRServiceLauncher.exe fails to restrict privileged process handle management.
target_node.postcondition: Attacker captures and utilizes an exposed privileged process handle, gaining full local privilege escalation to Administrator or SYSTEM permissions.

source_evidence.description: A remote web page could inject arbitrary HTML code into the Oculus Browser UI, allowing an attacker to spoof UI and potentially execute code. This affects the Oculus Browser starting from version 5.2.7 until 5.7.11.

Due to a bug with management of handles in OVRServiceLauncher.exe, an attacker could expose a privileged process handle to an unprivileged process, leading to local privilege escalation. This issue affects Oculus Desktop versions after 1.39 and prior to 31.1.0.67.507.
